title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Personnel
tiers.description: PDMRs and other Employees or consultants of the Group; the default population subject to the general prior-clearance and notification regime for Dealing in Company Securities.

tiers.name: PDMRs
tiers.description: Any Director or senior executive of the Company who has regular access to Inside Information and the power to make managerial decisions affecting the Company's future development and business prospects. PDMRs are absolutely prohibited from Dealing in financial products over Company Securities (including hedge arrangements) and from margin lending or similar secured arrangements, and have additional FCA notification and initial/ongoing/final disclosure obligations.

tiers.name: PCAs
tiers.description: Persons closely associated with a PDMR: a spouse or equivalent partner; a dependent child or stepchild under 18; a relative sharing the same household as the PDMR for at least a year; or a legal person, trust or partnership managed by, controlled by, or set up for the benefit of such a person. Sections 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 14 (clearance, notification, exceptional circumstances, trustee dealing) apply to PCAs via the PDMR's obligation to ensure they do not breach the Policy.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Relevant only to determine the Approving Officer: for a Director other than the Chair, the Chair is the Approving Officer; for the Chair, the CEO and one other Director act jointly; for non-Director Personnel, the CEO is the Approving Officer.

rules.detail: Absolute, permanent ban with no clearance route; carve-out only for an option over unissued capital granted by the Company itself.
rules.evidence: PDMRs are prohibited at all times from Dealing in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's Securities (including, but not limited to, hedge arrangements).

rules.detail: Non-PDMR Personnel are not subject to the absolute ban; Company Securities is defined to include financial products, derivatives and other financial instruments created over the Company's securities, so an OTC derivative is a Dealing requiring prior written clearance from the Approving Officer.
rules.evidence: Company Securities means all Securities in the Company or a Group member ... (including financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's Securities, derivatives or other financial instruments including phantom options).

rules.detail: Hedge arrangements are expressly named as an example of the prohibited financial products; no vesting distinction is drawn (there is no unvested/vested carve-out in this clause).

Dealing in Company Securities on behalf of the trust will not require clearance if the decision to Deal was taken by the other trustees (or by the trust's investment managers) independently of the member of Personnel.

an undertaking or election to take up entitlements under a rights issue or other offer (including an offer for Company Securities in lieu of a cash dividend); the take up of entitlements under a rights issue or other offer; and allowing entitlements to lapse under a rights issue or other offer, provided that the member of Personnel explains the reasons for the Dealing not taking place at another time and that the Approving Officer is satisfied with that explanation.

A member of Personnel can be permitted to transfer Company Securities between two accounts of that member of Personnel during a Closed Period, provided that such a transfer does not result in a change in price of the relevant Company Securities.

financing_disclosure: PDMR: initial disclosure to the Company Secretary, within 1 Business Day of appointment, of all contracts (other than with the Company) conferring a right to call for or deliver Company shares, debentures or scheme interests
PDMR: ongoing disclosure to the Company Secretary, within 1 Business Day of any change, of changes to such contracts
PDMR: final disclosure to the Company Secretary, within 1 Business Day of ceasing to be a PDMR, of such contracts

exemption_authority: The Approving Officer may grant a sale-only clearance during a Closed Period in Exceptional Circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order, or other overriding legal/regulatory requirement), limited to the number of shares needed and subject to no Inside Information and compliance with Article 19 of UK MAR; described as unlikely to be granted except in rare cases. No exemption exists from the PDMR's absolute, permanent prohibition on financial products/hedge arrangements or margin lending/similar secured arrangements in section 5.
jurisdiction_overlays: UK Market Abuse Regulation (retained UK MAR, as it forms part of English law)
FCA notification requirements for PDMRs and PCAs

bespoke_clauses.topic: PDMR absolute derivatives and secured-financing ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: PDMRs are prohibited at all times from Dealing in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's Securities (including, but not limited to, hedge arrangements). ... PDMRs are prohibited at all times from entering into margin lending or similar arrangements in respect to Company Securities they hold or in which they have a Relevant Interest.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both legs of a funded collar with a bank (the OTC put/call and the secured loan) are banned outright for any PDMR at all times, with no clearance mechanism, no vesting distinction and no listed exception route in Schedule 1 or 2 (those only cover ordinary share sales in Exceptional Circumstances).

bespoke_clauses.clause: For the avoidance of doubt this prohibition in relation to financial products does not apply to an option over unissued capital granted by the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Confirms the ban targets third-party/market derivatives like a bank collar, not the Company's own incentive option grants; it gives no comfort for a bank-written structure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sections 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 14 also apply to PCAs of PDMRs ... Section 5 (the absolute hedging/margin-lending ban) is not among the sections listed as extending to PCAs.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: On a literal reading, a PDMR's family trust or spouse (a PCA) is not directly bound by the absolute section 5 ban, only by the general clearance/notification regime; however the PDMR's own overriding duty to 'ensure that their PCAs do not breach this Policy' makes routing a collar through a PCA a live legal risk rather than a clean workaround.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Deal ... includes: ... using Company Securities as security for a loan or other obligation.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For senior employees who are not PDMRs, both the derivative legs and the secured loan of a collar are only 'Dealings' requiring ordinary prior clearance and post-trade notification, not an absolute ban, making a funded collar structurally possible for that population subject to Closed Periods and Approving Officer discretion.

bespoke_clauses.clause: from 1 January of each year until publication of the Company's annual financial report ... from 1 July of each year until publication of the Company's half-year financial report ... from first day of each Quarter until the publication of the Company's quarterly report
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because RSG reports quarterly, half-yearly and annually, and each Closed Period runs from the start of the period to publication (with a 30-day minimum for annual/half-year), open trading windows for entering or unwinding a collar are narrow and must be checked quarter by quarter.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The status of Trading Plans and Investment Programmes under the UK Market Abuse Regulation and, more particularly the ability of a member of Personnel to carry out transactions under a Trading Plan or an Investment Programme during Closed Periods, remains uncertain.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even for non-PDMR Personnel, the Company treats derivative or plan-based structures executing during a Closed Period as legally uncertain under UK MAR and takes a conservative approach, so a bank should expect execution to be confined to open windows.

summary: For a PDMR (director or senior executive with regular access to Inside Information), a funded collar with a bank is not possible: section 5 imposes an absolute, permanent, clearance-free prohibition on Dealing in any financial product created over or in respect of Company Securities (expressly including hedge arrangements) and on margin lending or similar secured arrangements, with no exception in Schedules 1 or 2. For other Personnel, both legs are only 'Dealings' under the broad definitions (which expressly cover derivatives, agreements to deal, and using shares as security for a loan), so a collar is structurally possible subject to prior written clearance from the Approving Officer (5 Business Day validity, 3 Business Day response), post-trade notification to the Company Secretary within 1 Business Day, and execution outside the frequent Closed Periods (which run from the start of each quarter/half-year/year until results are published, plus event-driven blackouts). Routing a PDMR's collar through a family member or trust (a PCA) is legally uncertain, since the absolute section 5 ban is not among the sections expressly extended to PCAs, but the PDMR's overriding duty to prevent PCA breaches makes this an unreliable workaround rather than a safe structuring route. No exemption authority exists for the section 5 ban; the only discretionary relief (Exceptional Circumstances) is limited to a sale-only clearance during a Closed Period and would not authorise a collar's derivative or loan legs in any event.
